Pixel Blade · brand direction · round one

Livery over garden.

Two layers, and they never mix. The garden is warm, deep, and emotional — it is what the visitor moves through. The livery is flat gold on dead black, exact to the hairline — it is what the visitor reads. Advertising is the first one. Execution is the second.

The idea

Blades are no longer steel. Pixels.

Spencer Lee

That line resolves the thing that was fighting itself last round. There is no corporate brand and emotional brand to reconcile — the split is the product. The feeling is what advertising sells; the precision is how it gets cut. A warrior in a garden is not a contradiction either. The garden is the discipline. The warrior is the capability. Neither is decoration.

So the identity is built as two layers that stay separate on purpose. Warm cinematic depth behind. Cold exact gold linework in front. The visitor moves through the first and reads the second, and the tension between them is the whole point.

Palette · livery

Non-metallic black, tan-leaning gold.

John Player Special ran gold mylar pinstripes and logos over a non-metallic black body — and the car numbers were tan paint, "more tan than gold." That single detail is what separates this from the aching-for-class law-firm black-and-gold. The black is flat. The gold is warm and slightly dull, not bright yellow.

Every value below was sampled out of the generated assets, not chosen off a swatch. Ratios are measured against the sumi ground.

Ground. Flat, faintly green-black — the garden's black, not a blue-black.

The brand. Matte tan gold. Passes for body text, not just accents — rare for a gold.

The mylar flash. Hover, focus, one live edge. Never a surface.

kin deep
#6F582F
2.90 : 1 · no text

Hairlines, rules, borders. Structurally load-bearing, never legible.

washi
#E8E3D6
15.29 : 1

Body copy. Warm paper white — never a cool grey, never pure white.

The hard constraint: gold on washi measures 1.91 : 1. It is unreadable on any light ground. This brand is dark or it is not itself — and every light-background context (an invoice, a Word doc, a client's slide template) needs a declared substitute rather than a hopeful gold. Worth deciding now, not later.

Marks · four directions

The crane, argued four ways.

Same palette, same black, four different theories of what the mark is. My reads are below each one — the two I'd carry forward are marked keep.

What I'd actually build: D's idea in A's hand. Take the blade-wing double-read and redraw it at a single uniform pinstripe weight, flat, no gradient, straight segments only. Then rebuild it as real vector geometry — everything here is a raster comp, and none of it survives being a favicon yet.

The garden · world plates

Feudal, warm, and a skyline that belongs.

These set the environment the site moves through. Note how little of each frame is lit — roughly eighty percent is black, which is exactly what makes room for gold linework on top without either layer fighting the other.

Rules that fall out of this

What the system inherits.

  • Two layers

    Garden colors never touch interface chrome. Livery colors never appear inside photography. If a token is doing both jobs, one of them is wrong.

  • Gold is ink

    Flat, one tone, no gloss, no bevel, no gradient, no metallic sheen. The moment gold looks like metal, this becomes a law firm.

  • Line before fill

    Hairline rules are the default material — coachlines, not boxes. A filled surface has to argue for itself.

  • No shadows

    One elevation step, sumi to sumi-raised. Depth comes from the photographic layer behind, never from a drop shadow in front.

  • Dark by default

    The gold fails on light grounds at 1.91:1. Light contexts get a declared substitute, not a hopeful gold.

  • Straight segments

    Geometry comes from folding. Hard vertices, straight runs, no blobs and no soft organic curves in any brand-level drawing.

  • Amber is light

    The lantern color marks a source of illumination. It is never a background, a button, or a fill.

Open

What I need from you.

  • 01
    Is this the right gold?

    #C5A05F is the tan-leaning JPS read. If you want it richer or closer to leaf, say which way and I'll re-derive the whole ramp from it.

  • 02
    A, D, or the hybrid?

    My recommendation is D's blade-wing double-read drawn in A's uniform pinstripe. Say the word and the next round is that one shape, iterated hard, then vectored.

  • 03
    Does the warrior appear, or only his garden?

    Plate 01 puts a person in frame. Plates 02 and 03 don't need one. A brand that never shows the figure is more disciplined; one that does is warmer. Both are defensible.

  • 04
    Typeface for the wordmark.

    This board is set in Bodoni Moda over Archivo — the didone hairlines are deliberately the same gesture as the coachline. That is a proposal, not a decision.

  • 05
    How far does the Japanese surface go?

    You said principle and surface both. Kanji in the interface, or only in the environment and the mark? That line needs drawing before components get built.
